title: A structurally malformed save can erase the live run while reporting success
evidence: Controlled corruption fixture: node.path=[[1]] passes _validate_save. load_game returns true and 'Game loaded.' after _apply_save raises an index error and leaves only node 1. Evidence: probes/corrupt_save.log; simulation_project/corrupt_save_results.json. Validator accepts version='999.0' and researched=['invalid_tech']; _is_unlocked later indexes TECH[t] without a guard. Evidence: simulation_results save_unknown_version/save_unknown_research. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: In an isolated copy, save a valid two-node run, replace a path point with [1], then Load. Related unvalidated required tunnel/packet/contract fields also pass the validator.
impact: Loading a parseable but damaged save changes live state before failure; the success message conceals lost structures.
recommendation: Validate every field and nested collection that _apply_save or simulation consumes; build a complete temporary restored state and commit it only after all coercion and invariants succeed. Declare supported save-schema versions, migrate known older versions and validate researched IDs before committing a temporary restored state.
acceptance: Malformed vector paths, missing required fields and wrong collection types are refused; the existing run remains byte-equivalent and Load returns false. Unsupported schemas and unknown researched IDs produce a clear error rather than a later lookup failure; supported legacy schemas migrate correctly.

title: Saved network topology, identities and numeric state are insufficiently validated
evidence: Controlled schema fixtures all return an empty validation error for hub→child→hub cycles, duplicate node.id and a connected node.tunnel='invalid'. Runtime consequences follow unchecked recursion/dictionary access in _calc_subtree and upkeep. Evidence: simulation_results save_cycle/save_duplicate_id/save_unknown_tunnel. A fixture with next_id=1, camera zoom=0 and compute=-100 is accepted with no validation error; _apply_save assigns these values directly. Evidence: simulation_results save_invalid_ranges. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Mutate a valid serialized fixture's parent graph, node IDs or tunnel key; call _validate_save. These are synthetic damaged saves, not a legal-play topology.
impact: An accepted save can overwrite the hub, recurse indefinitely, or fail the first simulation tick.
recommendation: Require unique matching node IDs/keys, one root hub, valid parents, acyclic parent chains, valid tunnel/path state for every link, and valid packet-route references. Require finite bounded numeric values, a next_id above all existing IDs, valid camera zoom, footprint bounds and sizes, and valid output/timer/lane values.
acceptance: Each invalid graph is rejected without applying it; a valid disconnected branch remains loadable. Reject colliding next_id, zero/invalid zoom and impossible numeric state before application; normal generated saves remain valid.

title: Saving over a parseable invalid file destroys the last-good backup
evidence: Controlled file fixture: create two valid saves, replace current save with {"version":"0.6.4"}, then Save. _read_valid_save(backup) changes from non-null to null. Rotation checks only JSON dictionary parsing, not _validate_save. Evidence: simulation_results invalid_backup_rotation. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Use isolated save paths; create a valid backup, corrupt current save with valid JSON lacking game state, then save the active run.
impact: The only recoverable previous run is replaced by semantically unusable data, so a later failed/corrupt current save has no recovery path.
recommendation: Rotate the current file only when the same full validator used for loading accepts it; preserve the previous backup otherwise.
acceptance: After saving over parseable invalid JSON, the previous backup remains valid and unchanged; ordinary valid rotation still works.

title: Keyboard focus escapes blocking modals and activates background controls
evidence: _grab_modal_focus assigns only the initial button. Actual Tab events in controls_probe move Settings Off→Off→Off→Code→100%→Close→Build→Tech→Stats. Enter press/release then changes ui.tab tostats while settings_visible remains true. No focus containment or background-control guard exists. Final source recheck: In-game modal focus helper still assigns the first button without forward/backward trapping. New menu-side modal also only assigns initial focus. Baseline actual key-event evidence remains qualified v064.
reproduction: Open Settings, press Tab six times, then activate a background tab; repeat focus traversal around pause/win boundaries.
impact: A blocking modal permits hidden/background UI actions, undermining input isolation and potentially exposing Load/Quit controls through keyboard traversal.
recommendation: Trap forward/backward focus within the topmost modal and prevent background UI actions while it is open.
acceptance: Tab/Shift+Tab wrap within Settings, Pause and Victory, including nested Settings; Enter/Space never activates controls behind the modal.

title: Add a small discover-and-compromise loop before automation
evidence: _handle_click routes tools directly to placement, and _try_place_node pays resources and creates an owned node immediately. Unowned map blocks have no host discovery or compromise state. The accepted discovery direction is future work, not a missing implemented requirement. This observation concerns the existing main game mode in the frozen snapshot. A separate Netrun prototype appeared after the cutoff and was not inspected or played in this review; check that work before implementing the proposal. Final source recheck: Placement still instantly creates an owned producer; discovery/acquisition states remain a proposal.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: choose a producer, click valid ground, then draw its tunnel; no target assessment occurs.
impact: The player's main decision reads as building a producer rather than gaining access to a hostile endpoint.
recommendation: Build the smallest accepted base: start on one persistent host in a visible city with unknown contents. Scan graph-adjacent hosts; reveal host type, security and compatible payloads. Hack one eligible host and gain persistence. Install an existing producer/processor as a payload on that host; its output supplies information/resources. Persistence, rather than installing a payload, enables the next adjacent scan. Group several hosts into one named organization. Prototype3-5 hosts and1-2 organizations before extending the economy.
acceptance: A fresh run completes scan -> reveal -> hack -> persistence -> optional payload -> scan further in five minutes. Unknown host interiors stay hidden; nonadjacent targets cannot be scanned; a newly persistent empty host can reveal its neighbours. Organization membership is legible, and acquisition/production have separate states.

title: Teach a sustainable Cycles backbone before expanding Intel sales
evidence: _next_step asks for a Phishing Kit before checking any Cycles source. has_producer includes Intel producers, so its later producer check cannot teach Cycles sustainability. acceptance: Fresh-start guidance requests a productive linked Cycles host; once sustained, it advances to Intel and Cash, and returns to recovery advice if Cycles income stops.

title: Save rotation ignores copy and deletion failures before removing the current file
evidence: save_game removes an existing backup, ignores the return from copy_absolute, removes the current save, then attempts rename_absolute. Only the final rename is checked. No OS I/O-failure injection was performed. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Source review; relevant situations are a locked file, denied backup write or a filesystem error during rotation.
impact: A failed backup copy can discard both the old backup and current save before the new file is installed.
recommendation: Check each filesystem result, preserve at least one valid old file until replacement succeeds, and report the failed stage. Use a checked replace/rename strategy appropriate to the platform.
acceptance: Injected copy/replace failures return false and leave a valid loadable current or backup file; success is reported only after final replacement is readable.

title: Save/load changes node iteration order and therefore deterministic threat selection
evidence: Controlled valid roundtrip: nodes inserted [1,2,10], equal-depth sweep targets2 before save; JSON.stringify sorts object keys, load rebuilds nodes [1,10,2], next sweep targets10. recommendation: Use stable numeric node ordering in order-sensitive simulation loops or serialize/restore explicit ordering; specify deterministic sweep tie-breaking.

title: Outbound processor-input packets can follow an obsolete rerouted chain
evidence: Controlled topology fixture: C2→node2→Forge3 input route[2,3]; reroute Forge3 to C2 while packet is on edge2. Packet survives with idx=1, route[2,3] although Forge3.parent=1. Stale-hop check only checks dir==1. Evidence: simulation_results stale_downward_route. recommendation: Validate adjacency in both directions and invalidate packets whenever any stored edge's endpoints no longer match the route snapshot.
acceptance: Upbound and downbound packets are canceled on changed route adjacency; unchanged packets still arrive exactly once.

title: Disabling a forwarding structure silences its live tunnel without stopping transit

title: Contract board rebuild destroys keyboard focus after accepting a job

title: Linked-structure contract text omits which nodes qualify

evidence: Controlled rates fixture at100%: net-rate rectx312,y42,w409 and legend rectx600,y42,w519 intersect. Text is 'Cycles -99.9/s Intel +1000.0/s Cash +150.0/s ETA0:06'.
