The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Run a productive mixed network, or use the controlled three-rate fixture; both net rates and legend use fixed positions on the same row.
impact: Income and resource identity text become unreadable precisely when the economy is busy.
recommendation: Lay out rates and legend in a shared responsive container, separate rows or collapsible sections rather than independent fixed positions.
acceptance: All displayed rates, ETA and legend remain non-overlapping for large positive/negative rates at every text scale.

title: The Stats resource inventory omits Research
evidence: Controlled fixture with77 Research: stats_label lists Cycles,Intel,Crypto,Tools,Cash but no Research. Header contains77 Research. Evidence: probes/hud_v065_results.json stats_research and screenshot10_stats.png. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Earn Research through contracts/Lab, then open Stats.
impact: The supposedly comprehensive inventory excludes the resource needed for technology decisions.
recommendation: Add Research using the same inventory presentation and precision policy as other resources.
acceptance: Stats shows all six resource balances and matches the HUD after research spending, rewards and loading.

title: An overload alert selects the structure instead of its diagnostic tunnel
evidence: Controlled overloaded-edge fixture: _jump_alert('overload') sets selected_id=2, selected_tunnel=-1. The tunnel inspector contains offered/cap/loss diagnostics; the selected producer inspector does not show that edge detail. Evidence: probes/hud_v065_results.json overload_jump. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Click an OVERLOADED tunnel alert.
impact: The alert moves to the location but opens the less useful inspector, requiring another precise map click to understand the issue.
recommendation: Select the overloaded tunnel or open an explicit throughput diagnostic section for that edge. Provide contextual upgrade/reroute actions and show the expected capacity/cost change from the selected diagnostic tunnel.
acceptance: One alert click opens the affected link's capacity/offered/loss information and keeps coherent selection state.

title: Quarantined intact branches are labeled OFFLINE / unlinked in aggregate alerts
evidence: Controlled intact linked node with quarantine=5 is excluded from _connected; the alert text is '1 structure(s) OFFLINE / unlinked'. The inspector has a distinct quarantine state but the aggregate alert collapses causes. Evidence: probes/hud_v065_results.json quarantine_alert. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Allow ICE to quarantine a connected host without cutting its link.
impact: The prominent alert suggests a wiring problem even though the physical branch remains intact and recovery is time-based.
recommendation: Separate quarantined and unlinked counts, or describe the mixed alert as inactive and reveal cause per target.
acceptance: An ICE-quarantined branch is visibly distinguished from a missing link in both the aggregate alert and inspector.

title: String-based message detection loses repeated and same-frame action results
evidence: Reverified v0.6.5: emit the same failed placement, wait 3.7 s, emit again; _msg_t stays 0 and status remains Hover hint. In a second controlled case, assign two results before one UI update; history contains only the second. The new queue stores observed strings but cannot recover undetected events. Evidence: probes/hud_v065_results.json repeated_same_message/same_frame_history. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Repeat an identical invalid action after feedback expires, or produce two independent results within one render frame.
impact: Repeated input appears ignored, and earlier same-frame rewards/failures vanish before entering the new history.
recommendation: Emit action results as explicit events with unique IDs rather than watching a shared string; enqueue each event at its source.
acceptance: Every action result is captured, including identical consecutive failures and two events in one frame; history and visible feedback preserve both.

title: The severity queue can delay urgent blackout warnings behind routine messages
evidence: v0.6.5 classifies severity and varies color/duration, but uses FIFO pop_front. A controlled 10-routine-message fixture queues BLACKOUT last, giving a 22 s wait before its 3.6 s display. After 100 more messages, the pending queue grows to 110 while history is bounded at 12. Evidence: probes/hud_v065_results.json warning_fifo/queue_bound. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Make several rapidly changing routine selections/results, then receive an ICE blackout or another critical error.
impact: Urgent information can arrive after the four-second blackout has already finished, while old routine feedback continues.
recommendation: Preempt or prioritize urgent operational events; coalesce routine repeats and bound the pending queue by count/age. Preserve readable acknowledgements without replaying obsolete actions.
acceptance: A newly received critical warning displays immediately; routine backlog remains bounded and does not delay time-critical information.

title: Planning pause has no persistent visible indicator after its status message expires
evidence: Controlled planning pause fixture: paused=true, pause_overlay.visible=false; after3.1s status='Hover hint' and header has noPaused marker. Evidence: probes/hud_v065_results.json planning_pause. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Use planning pause, then hover a host or wait for the status timer.
impact: Players can mistake a deliberately paused simulation for stalled production or broken input.
recommendation: Show a persistent PAUSED/planning badge with a clear Resume action while keeping the map interactive.
acceptance: Planning pause remains visibly indicated until resumed, independent of tool hints or action messages; opening/closing menus preserves the badge correctly.

title: Loading a run preserves queued messages from the discarded timeline
evidence: A controlled v0.6.5 UI fixture queues old reward/expired messages, applies a valid saved state via the same _apply_save path used by Load, then reports Game loaded. The old reward still displays, with old expiry and Game loaded pending behind it. _apply_save clears Main transients but not UI message state. Evidence: probes/hud_v065_results.json load_message_timeline. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Queue rapid action results, then successfully Load another saved run before the message queue drains. The fixture drives _apply_save directly to isolate message lifecycle.
impact: A restored run shows obsolete rewards/failures from a timeline that no longer exists, and Load success itself may be delayed.
recommendation: Reset pending/current UI messages and align history with the successful load boundary; immediately surface the load/recovery result. Preserve messages when Load is refused.
acceptance: After a successful Load, no discarded-timeline event is shown as current; success/recovery displays immediately, while failed Load leaves live-state feedback intact.

title: Armed tunnel and Proxy tools still miss visible tower roofs
evidence: The isolated headless probe finds C2 at roof point (74,20) through _node_at_silhouette, while _node_at(cell(3,0)) returns -1 and an armed tunnel reports 'Click a node.' Default selection has the B48 silhouette fix; tunnel and Proxy tools still use footprint-only hit tests. main/minimap hashes match the later source_v065 snapshot. Final source recheck: _try_tunnel and _try_convert_relay still call _node_at(cell); the new rerouting path also uses the same footprint target policy. Prior headless roof-hit proof remains applicable.
reproduction: Use map_project/map_probe.gd, or arm a source tunnel and click the elevated part of C2 outside its ground footprint. Proxy conversion has the same footprint-only target path.
impact: A target that visibly responds to inspection becomes unclickable during the operation requiring it, especially on tall structures.
recommendation: Resolve a single visible-node target for inspect, tunnel endpoints and Proxy conversion, keeping ground-footprint placement rules separate.
acceptance: Roof and footprint clicks choose the same visible frontmost node in all three modes; clicking empty ground still performs no node operation.

title: Undo can leave a stationary route preview showing an obsolete route
evidence: map_probe_results.json records a cached valid 12-cell route to a second Mirai at (13,4). After Undo removes that target, pending source and pointer key stay unchanged; cached preview still says valid/12 while a fresh calculation returns blocked/INF. Cache keys contain only cell, pending source and tool. Final source recheck: Cache key still uses only cell, pending source and tool. Undo target removal/restore still does not invalidate this cache; new reroute Undo also clears only _pl_cache.
reproduction: Run map_project/map_probe.gd, or preview a route while planning-paused and undo another node/tunnel affecting that route without moving the pointer.
impact: The planning display can retain a nonexistent path or incorrect route cost until the player moves the mouse.
recommendation: Include a topology revision in the preview cache key or invalidate it on every placement, removal, restore and reroute.
acceptance: With a stationary pointer, Undo/redo-equivalent restores, dismantling and route changes refresh validity, geometry and cost before the next click.

title: Empty-cell route endpoints can display OK but cannot be committed
evidence: _preview_route falls back to _find_path_to_cell for an empty hovered cell and returns blocked=false when geometry is routable. _update_hint displays [OK], but _try_tunnel rejects every endpoint without a node. Final source recheck: Empty-cell fallback can still return blocked=false and OK while commit requires an existing node.
reproduction: Arm a source, hover a reachable empty street and observe its white route/OK hint; clicking that same cell reports 'Click a node.' This is source-grounded, not a recorded physical click.
impact: The preview signals a complete valid operation at points where the actual action is unavailable.
recommendation: Distinguish 'route can reach here' from 'valid endpoint'; highlight commit-ready node targets and show 'choose a node' on empty endpoints.
acceptance: Only an eligible distinct node target is marked ready to commit; exploratory geometry may remain visible with a clearly incomplete state.

title: Proxy tunnel previews overstate upkeep by 2.5 times
evidence: The isolated probe uses an actual one-cell route from a converted Proxy: _update_hint predicts 0.05 Cycles/s for DNS, while committing and ticking computes 0.02 Cycles/s. Preview multiplies length by protocol upkeep without the Proxy's 0.4 factor. Final source recheck: Tunnel preview still uses length*UPKEEP; actual Proxy source upkeep still applies 0.4. Post-build reserve forecast is in the structure branch only.
reproduction: Run map_project/map_probe.gd, or preview and build a route from a converted Proxy and compare the preview estimate with the network upkeep change.
impact: Players overestimate the cost of the infrastructure intended to make expansion economical.
recommendation: Use one shared effective-upkeep calculation in the preview and simulation.
acceptance: Every protocol preview matches actual incremental upkeep for both ordinary sources and converted Proxies to displayed precision.

title: The top HUD can trigger unintended upward edge-panning
evidence: Edge-pan checks mp.x>=300 and mp.y<=22 regardless of whether the pointer is over the resource HUD. That HUD covers the map's top 64 pixels, so pointing at the top resource row can move the camera. Final source recheck: Edge-pan still triggers y<=22 when x>=300, including the top HUD.
reproduction: Move the pointer into the resource bar's first 22 pixels to the right of the left panel and wait while no modal is open.
impact: Reading resources can move the map and disrupt the placement or inspection context.
recommendation: Define edge-pan zones on the unobscured map rectangle and suppress them while interacting with HUD controls; allow edge-pan to be disabled.
acceptance: Hovering any HUD element leaves the camera still; pointer movement to a real map-edge pan zone scrolls as documented.

title: Minimap view rectangle includes world hidden behind the UI
evidence: The view rectangle uses the full viewport width/height, although the left 300 pixels and top HUD hide world content. The actual opening layout is 1280x720 with a 300-pixel panel and 64-pixel top bar. Final source recheck: Minimap outline still uses the full viewport, including the covered left panel and top HUD.
reproduction: At a middle-map camera position, compare the outlined minimap area with the world that is actually visible outside the left panel and HUD.
impact: The overview claims areas are in view when they are covered by controls, making click-to-pan and boundary inspection less precise.
recommendation: Calculate the world bounds of the unobscured map rectangle and use them for the minimap view indicator and centring policy.
acceptance: Each corner of the minimap view outline corresponds to a visible map corner, including after resize and zoom.

title: ICE tracers cut across buildings instead of following their real tunnels
evidence: Normal links use _edge_pts routed polylines, but the ICE warning draws straight node-centre lines and interpolates its moving marker between centres. The sweep's counterplay checks the actual parent links. Final source recheck: Threat warning lines and tracer still interpolate directly between node centres rather than _edge_pts.
reproduction: Trigger a sweep on a branch whose tunnel takes a street detour; the threat overlay uses the direct chord instead of the routed street path.
impact: The visual threat appears on a different part of the map from the session the player needs to cut or reroute.
recommendation: Draw the warning and position the tracer using the swept edge's existing route polyline, while preserving pause-safe hop timing.
acceptance: At every hop the threat marker and warning line lie on the same visible tunnel as packet traffic, including detours and parallel lanes.

title: Short-link labels are covered by the structures they describe
evidence: Screenshots 05_first_link.png and 06_selected_producer.png show the one-cell DNS label running beneath the overlapping C2/Mirai silhouettes. Labels are drawn at the polyline midpoint before structures are painted, with no collision placement or backing. Final source recheck: Link labels still paint before structures at the route midpoint with no collision handling/backing. Prior short-link screenshot evidence remains mechanically relevant.
reproduction: Follow the recorded legal opening: Mirai at [2,5] linked to C2 [2,2]; inspect the route label in screenshots 05 and 06.
impact: The first working link's latency/health annotation is difficult to read even at the default scale, undermining the feedback meant to teach routing.
recommendation: Move short-link annotations to a non-overlapping badge or selected-link callout with a dark backing; avoid labelling every crowded edge simultaneously.
acceptance: The recorded opening's full link label remains legible over both roofs, and a dense network does not create overlapping unreadable labels.

title: Fog blocks and legal placement disagree at vision boundaries
evidence: Fog marks a whole 4x4 block visible from one centre-cell test, while placement checks every footprint cell with exact radius distance. Around a radius-16 C2 at (2.5,2.5), a fog-visible block can include cells beyond that radius, and a dark block can include legal cells. Final source recheck: Fog still marks whole 4x4 blocks from one centre-cell test while placement checks every footprint cell against exact radius.
reproduction: Source-derived boundary example: block x16..19/y0..3 tests centre (18.5,2.5) as visible, although its x19 cell centres are outside the radius. Move a producer preview across such a boundary.
impact: Illuminated terrain can reject placement for being outside vision, and actionable boundary cells can appear unavailable.
recommendation: Use a consistent cell-level accessibility mask for fog/placement or explicitly display the exact build-reach boundary over coarse atmospheric fog.
acceptance: A player can determine whether the entire preview footprint is within access from the map cue; no fully legal footprint is visually marked unavailable.

title: Same-seed restores can leave minimap host markers at old positions
evidence: Controlled rendered cache-invalidation probe restored a same-seed state with equal node count/camera but synthetically moved C2 to(18,18); minimap emitted zero draw notifications. C2 does not ordinarily move. Its key covers seed/count/relay count/camera, not node identity or positions. The legal analogous scenario is same-count saves with different producer positions; that exact legal roundtrip was not recorded. Evidence: render_results.json same_seed_node_move_load.
reproduction: Restore two same-seed states with equal node and relay counts but different positions, keeping camera and zoom unchanged.
impact: Players navigate toward markers belonging to the discarded run.
recommendation: Invalidate on restore and include a node-position/topology revision in minimap state tracking.
acceptance: Same-count replacement, Undo and save restore repaint markers immediately without needing a camera move.

title: Advertised capacity behaves as a soft loss parameter rather than a throughput ceiling
evidence: Measured controlled fixture: DNS cap3, offered4, distance loss0.03 produces modeled delivered3.2133/s. At extreme overload the0.9 loss ceiling lets arbitrarily large offered load exceed capacity. This is an observed model choice, not a proven design-intent bug. Evidence: simulation_results capacity_soft_ceiling. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Compare _edge.cap and _edge.delivered on an overloaded DNS trunk. Prior acceptance checks did not require a hard cap.
impact: Players cannot infer what a3-packet/s link can actually carry; node throughput ceilings cease to be ceilings.
recommendation: Either enforce an actual delivery/admission ceiling with queue/drop behavior, or explicitly call the displayed value a soft bandwidth/loss rating and teach that model.
acceptance: For a hard-cap design, sustained delivery never exceeds declared capacity; for a soft model, inspector and help text clearly state the nonlinear rule.

title: Prevent or explain Overclock spending on currently unavailable producers
evidence: Controlled fixtures: disabled Mirai and disconnected Mirai both spend20 Cycles and receive boost_t20; disabled production is{}, disconnected chain is[]. Evidence: simulation_results disabled_overclock/offline_overclock. Spending on an unavailable target is verified, but requiring a live target or queuing a boost is a design choice, not an established forbidden operation. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Select a disabled or offline producer and press Overclock; the timer runs while it cannot deliver additional production.
impact: A contextual action consumes scarce starting resources despite no current benefit, with no confirmation of a queued strategy.
recommendation: Gate the command on operational positive-output state or explicitly offer a queued boost that begins when the host is online. Show the reason when unavailable.
acceptance: Disabled/offline/0%-output targets cannot silently spend20 Cycles on an expiring unusable boost; operational targets retain the existing behavior.

title: Exit and Load actions replace unsaved progress without a save decision
evidence: Menu buttons call go_main_menu, quit_game and load_game directly; go_main_menu/quit_game switch/exit immediately and no autosave or dirty-run decision is implemented. This proposal concerns the user flow, separate from save format/validation defects. Final source recheck: Menu/Pause exits and Load still call session replacement directly, with no unsaved decision. Startup preference persistence is separate from run saving.
reproduction: Change the network after the last manual save, then choose Main Menu, Quit or Load Game from the Menu/Pause UI.
impact: A single menu action can discard the player's latest network changes without revealing that outcome.
recommendation: Track unsaved progress and offer Save/Discard/Cancel before destructive session replacement; keep the flow concise when the run is already saved.
acceptance: A dirty run can be saved or retained before exit/load; Cancel restores the same run and focus, while an already-saved run exits without redundant prompts.

title: Inspector actions sit after long flavour text and technical details
evidence: info_body precedes every action and begins with d.homage; critical Status is appended near its end. In the200% probe the body ends y1335, first action starts1341 and rate controls start1542 inside a scroll viewport ending667. Actions remain scrollable, but require traversing the entire prose block. This is separate from the global status-line height finding. Final source recheck: Long inspector body still precedes all controls and status remains near the bottom. New Reroute adds another below-body action; do not reuse old action pixel coordinates as freshly measured v066 geometry.
reproduction: Select a producer at200% text and attempt to quickly disable it or reduce output during a network problem.
impact: Time-sensitive controls and operational status are far below descriptive prose.
recommendation: Put state and main operational controls near the top or in a bounded persistent action area; move flavour/extended metrics into a secondary section.
acceptance: Disable/output actions and current status are quickly reachable from the initial inspector position at all scales; full descriptive details remain available.

title: Overclock lacks cost, duration and remaining-boost context
evidence: The action label is only ⚡ Overclock(O), with empty tooltip. main.gd defines20 Cycles/20 seconds and sets boost_t, but inspector shows no remaining duration or active boost label; probe boost_time20 is visible only as a doubled Produces value. Functional disabled/offline overclock guards are owned by the simulation audit. Final source recheck: Overclock still has only its short label and no cost/duration/remaining boost preview. Canonical operational-state text does not add that context.
reproduction: Select a producer, inspect Overclock before using it, then return to that producer during its20-second boost.
impact: Players spend a resource without a preview and cannot tell when the temporary effect will end or whether another press is useful.
recommendation: Display the cost and effect duration before activation, then show boost state/countdown and current affordability.
acceptance: The control explains20 Cycles→2× output for20s and shows remaining boost time; a resource shortage has an explicit reason.

title: The inspector lacks actual throughput and delivery rates
evidence: Baseline inspector reports nominal generation/processor recipe values rather than measured delivery. The final snapshot adds operational-state labels and effective tunnel admission capacity; those improvements are credited. Actual per-host throughput, deliveries and losses still require inference from packet motion and stock changes. Baseline UI evidence is controlled; current persistence is source-rechecked.
reproduction: Inspect a disabled producer or a connected processor with no Intel/fuel, then compare the displayed rate with actual traffic.
impact: Players cannot judge what a disabled node could recover or why an apparently rated processor is idle.
recommendation: Separate rated capacity, current production/processing, delivered throughput and a concise idle/limited reason; retain capacity information while disabled.
acceptance: An idle processor identifies the limiting input/fuel/route; a disabled producer retains rated capacity while current output is0; delivery loss is not presented as raw production.

title: Tunnel latency uses packet units for a route-length count
evidence: The inspector labels _edge_len as Latency:N pkt, but main.gd:735–737 returns path.size(), a cell count. Packet motion depends on PACKET_SPEED/slow_factor, so this count does not directly communicate elapsed delivery time. Final source recheck: Latency still labels _edge_len/path-size as pkt. Effective admission-capacity improvement is a separate metric and must be credited.
reproduction: Inspect a short and long tunnel and try to infer when a packet will reach the parent from the displayed latency.
impact: The central timing metric has an unclear unit and cannot be readily related to travel time.
recommendation: Label route length in cells/tiles and provide an estimated travel time in seconds using the actual path/speed, with variable slowdown qualified.
acceptance: Every displayed metric has a coherent unit; players can compare route length and approximate link travel time without interpreting 'packet latency'.

title: Dismantle does not preview the affected branch or refund outcome
evidence: The button is labelled Dismantle(Del) with no impact tooltip. main._remove_node removes the selected node and detaches incoming children; dismantling does not call _refund, while Ctrl+Z restores the removed topology. Final source recheck: Dismantle still lacks branch/refund/undo impact preview. Reroute now exists as an alternative operational action; do not imply removal is the sole available change.
reproduction: Select a relay/processor with incoming branches and inspect Dismantle before activating it.
impact: Players cannot see how many structures lose their C2 route or whether build resources return before the action.
recommendation: Show affected direct/descendant nodes, resource outcome and undo availability near Dismantle; distinguish removing a node from removing its outbound tunnel.
acceptance: Before removal the inspector explains the resulting disconnected branch and refund policy; the subsequent undo restores the described topology.

title: Offer an immediate visible preview of palette tool details
evidence: _on_hover updates hover_tool and _update_info builds the detailed body, but _process shows sel_scroll only for selection or current_tool, not hover_tool. Probe hovering nest records its homage/cost in info_body while inspector_visible=false. Standard delayed tooltip is still present; the separate immediate detail preview is the broken part. The existing delayed tooltip already exposes full help; this proposal improves presentation rather than claiming hover help is absent. Final source recheck: show_info still excludes hover_tool, but complete delayed tooltip remains. Retain as immediate-hover-preview improvement/dead-preview cleanup, not absence of hover help.
reproduction: With no armed tool or selection, open Build and hover Mirai Dropper; inspect info_body and sel_scroll visibility.
impact: A player must wait for the tooltip; the existing immediate inspector-preview assignment is invisible while the build palette is open.
recommendation: Provide a visible compact hover preview that does not hide the hovered palette, or remove dead hover-inspector state and improve the tooltip intentionally.
acceptance: Hover/focus any tool exposes its help without first arming it, and the palette remains available under the pointer.

title: Locked tools do not name the research needed to unlock them
evidence: Tool tooltip is name+homage+cost; disabled state is based solely on _is_unlocked. No required technology is displayed or linked. For example Poisoned Package is disabled although the corresponding technology is named Supply-Chain Attacks. Final source recheck: Locked tool tooltip still lacks required technology; unlock-state processing unchanged.
reproduction: Start a new game, hover locked Poisoned Package, then compare the Tech list.
impact: Players must infer a differently named technology before they can act.
recommendation: Add a readable Locked—requires <technology> line and a route to that research card; retain readable names and costs while locked.
acceptance: Each locked tool identifies the exact technology and prerequisite chain; a player can navigate to the relevant card in one action.

title: Build costs give no live affordability or resource shortfall
evidence: Palette cost labels are set once to _cost_str; _process refreshes unlock state only. An unlocked tool with insufficient Cash/Intel has the same palette presentation as an affordable one. Final source recheck: Palette costs remain static and show no per-resource affordability deficits. Armed-tool hint now forecasts Cycles after build and warns about recovery reserve; credit this and narrow the proposal to preselection palette/remaining resource shortages.
reproduction: Research Cloud Cryptojacking, leave Cash below60, and compare its palette row before and after accumulating the required Cash.
impact: Placement failures are discovered after arming and selecting a map location.
recommendation: Show affordable/shortfall state beside each cost, while allowing intentional preview even when a resource is missing.
acceptance: A missing resource is named with its deficit and updates as stock changes; research lock and resource shortage are visually/textually distinct.

title: Palette does not expose production and processor operating recipes
evidence: Tool rows contain name and initial build cost only; tooltip contains homage. Actual producer rates and CONV input/output/fuel data in main.gd:21–37 appear only after selection of an installed structure. Final source recheck: Palette still shows name/cost and qualitative homage rather than production/processing recipes. New selected-state/effective-capacity text does not add pre-build recipe comparison.
reproduction: Compare Mirai vsCloud Cryptojacker, or Intel Lab vsExploit Forge before constructing them.
impact: Players cannot evaluate expected yield or recurring fuel needs when making the build decision.
recommendation: Add a compact functional summary: output resource/rate for producers and input→output/rate plus fuel for processors, with coverage modifiers explicitly qualified.
acceptance: Before arming a tool its base output or conversion recipe and recurring fuel are available in readable text, independently of icon colour.

title: Tunnel options lack a comparable set of operating metrics
evidence: Links rows show build cost; tooltip uses qualitative homage such as small/cheap/silent or fast/loud. Numeric capacity, upkeep/tile, trace/s and distance loss are in main.gd:58–64 and are not provided together for comparison. Final source recheck: Links palette still lacks consistent numeric comparisons. Selected tunnel now shows protocol/effective capacity, but that does not populate palette capacity/upkeep/trace/loss comparison.
reproduction: Open Build→Links and compare DNS Tunnel, VPN Tunnel and Reverse Shell before arming.
impact: Players choose tunnels by flavour and discover the actual cost/capacity consequences after deployment.
recommendation: Provide an aligned comparison or consistent tooltip fields for capacity, upkeep, trace and distance loss.
acceptance: Each tunnel exposes the same units/fields; players can compare a cheap route, cooling route and high-capacity route without placing them.

title: Custom palette buttons need explicit accessible names
evidence: _tool_entry creates a Button with empty text and places tool names in child Labels; no explicit accessibility name/description is set in this construction. The probe confirms every tool button_text is empty. This is a proposed accessibility hardening, not a claimed screen-reader runtime failure. Final source recheck: Custom tool Buttons still have empty own text and no explicit accessibility name; retain proposal status until platform announcement is tested.
reproduction: Inspect a palette button's own label/accessibility metadata and test keyboard/screen-reader navigation on the supported platform.
impact: Accessible announcement of the custom row is dependent on engine child-text inference rather than an explicit contract.
recommendation: Assign the button an explicit accessible name and description containing its tool name, role, cost and lock reason, using the supported Godot accessibility API.
acceptance: The platform screen reader announces a unique name, cost and availability for each tool; child labels do not cause duplicate announcements.

title: Research cards do not identify the exact unlocked tool
evidence: _tech_row shows t.name and t.desc but never renders t.unlocks. Several labels differ from the palette names, for example Onion Routing→Onion Route and Exploit Development→Exploit Forge. Final source recheck: Research rows still show name/desc/action without explicit unlocked palette names.
reproduction: Read a Tech card and locate the tool it will enable in Build.
impact: Players cannot reliably connect research investment to a concrete action or build category.
recommendation: Render Unlocks: <tool name> with the matching glyph/category and optionally a jump action.
acceptance: Every technology lists the exact current palette names it unlocks before purchase and after it is researched.

title: Disabled research purchases lack a local balance and shortfall
evidence: When prerequisites are satisfied b.disabled depends on resources.research<t.cost, while text remains Research (<cost>RP). No local current balance, remaining amount or tooltip is set. Final source recheck: Eligible unaffordable research still shows cost only and disables the button without local current balance/deficit.
reproduction: Open Tech with0RP, then with9RP, and compare an eligible10RP card.
impact: The player gets a disabled control without a clear local explanation of how close the unlock is.
recommendation: Add Research <current>/<required> and Need <deficit> messaging, plus a direct explanation of earning Research when the balance is zero. Show the Research price even when a prerequisite locks the card, alongside the named prerequisite and current balance.
acceptance: At9/10RP a10RP card states1RP missing; at10RP it becomes actionable immediately, and prerequisite lock remains a distinct status. Prerequisite-locked cards expose their price, and insufficient-balance cards expose the precise deficit.

title: Completed contracts have no notification outside the Jobs tab
evidence: The Jobs tab label is static; completion feedback exists only in card status/Claim button. main.gd:1988–1990 marks done and changes version without setting message. Probe completion retained message='baseline' even though done=true. Final source recheck: Completed feedback remains inside Jobs; main marks done without emitting completion message, and tab has no badge. New Decline/filtering does not notify completion.
reproduction: Accept a job, switch to Build/Tech, meet the objective and observe the navigation/status UI.
impact: Earned rewards can remain undiscovered and occupy contract slots while the player works elsewhere.
recommendation: Add a claimable-count badge and a concise completion event with a direct jump to the completed card.
acceptance: Completion is signalled from any tab once per job; the badge remains until reward claim and opens the relevant claim action.

title: Claimable and active jobs can be hidden below unopened offers
evidence: _rebuild_jobs iterates main.contracts in arrival order. Three cards are supported, but claimable/urgent state does not alter ordering or provide a view filter; at200% only a fraction of the first card is visible in screenshot17_jobs_200.png. Final source recheck: Card order remains main.contracts arrival order. Unwanted offers can now be declined; do not claim offers are irremovable. Claimable/active prioritization or badge grouping still absent.
reproduction: Keep the first offer unaccepted, accept the third, complete it, then revisit Jobs at large text size.
impact: The most actionable work requires scrolling past untouched offers, compounding the absence of external completion feedback.
recommendation: Offer Claimable/Active/Offers grouping or a pinned claimable summary while preserving stable card focus and IDs. Show a consistent positive countdown until expiry, then an explicit expired state; add labelled urgency for near deadlines without relying on colour alone.
acceptance: Claimable rewards and active deadlines are discoverable before unopened offers; changing state does not unexpectedly move keyboard focus. Accepted jobs are easy to locate, never display expired-looking zero while still active, and clearly distinguish urgent, expired and claimable states.

title: Production rates for Crypto, Tools and Research are absent from the rate HUD
evidence: v0.6.5 UI only loops rates overcompute,data,credits although resources/rates support all six keys. Controlled probe supplies Crypto12/s,Tools0.6/s,Research0.5/s and none appear in the net-rate text. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Run a skimmer, Forge or Research Lab and inspect the rate line.
impact: Players must watch stockpile increments to understand whether secondary resource chains are working.
recommendation: Make per-resource net rates available for every resource, using compact chips, tooltips or a Stats rates table to avoid expanding the crowded header.
acceptance: A player can read Crypto,Tools andResearch net production without inferring it from changing totals; zero-rate treatment is consistent.

title: A one-second wallet change is presented as sustainable income and goal ETA
evidence: Main samples resources minus previous stock over~1s; the UI immediately converts Cash rate into ETA and _peak_cash_rate uses the same samples. Contract payouts, purchases, refunds and ICE losses are mixed with operating delivery. Source reviewed; no long-run ETA accuracy experiment claimed. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Claim a Cash reward or buy an expensive structure between samples, then inspect rate/ETA; compare with a steady resource-delivery network.
impact: A one-off payout can briefly imply a near-immediate victory; construction can make a healthy network appear to have negative production.
recommendation: Keep wallet-change feedback but estimate sustainable delivery/consumption rates separately with a short smoothed window and exclude capital/reward events from production ETA.
acceptance: One-off transactions appear as transactions; production rate/ETA remains stable unless operational throughput changes, with an explicit insufficient-data state.

title: Stats reports stockpiles and counts without showing network operating efficiency
evidence: Stats shows Structures,Tunnels,In transit,Upkeep,Feed and stockpiles but no aggregate generated-versus-delivered rates, drops or net Cycles sustainability. Individual tunnel/inspector issues belong to the other UX agent. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Open Stats when the network is starved or overloaded and try to identify whether output covers upkeep.
impact: The network summary cannot distinguish an idle economy from a productive but lossy or uneconomic one.
recommendation: Add compact aggregate production, delivered throughput, dropped fraction and Cycles production/upkeep balance; keep detailed per-host diagnostics in the inspector.
acceptance: Stats can answer whether the network is producing, delivering and sustaining upkeep using actual measured events.

title: Repeated alert clicks always select the first failing structure
evidence: Controlled fixture with two offline nodes: _jump_alert('offline') selects node 2 on both clicks. Source breaks on first matching node every time. Evidence: probes/hud_v065_results.json repeated_alert_jump. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Create multiple offline/overloaded branches and repeatedly click their count alert.
impact: An aggregate alert offers no efficient route to the second or later issue and repeatedly pulls the camera back to the same host.
recommendation: Cycle through matching targets or open a short issue list, preserving a stable ordering and count.
acceptance: Every outstanding issue can be reached from its aggregate alert without manual searching; removed/repaired targets are skipped.

title: Starvation and critical-trace alerts lead to generic C2 text rather than a cause
evidence: _jump_alert falls back tohub_id forstarved/trace; the C2 inspector primarily contains flavor/zone information. It does not open a causal resource, noise or counteraction breakdown. Source-confirmed navigation. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Click Network STARVED or Trace CRITICAL.
impact: The advertised 'jump to the problem' action reaches C2 but leaves players to work out the remedy.
recommendation: Open a relevant diagnostic summary: Cycles balance/top upkeep routes for starvation, and noise sources/available counteractions for trace.
acceptance: Each alert exposes at least one concrete cause and an available next action, with links to implicated branches.

title: Long passive guidance consumes much of the usable sidebar at large text sizes
evidence: Viewed screenshot18_stats_200.png; measured at200%: next-step status is250px high whileStats scroll area is235px. The status Label autowraps as an unbounded child outside scroll containers. Evidence: probes/hud_v065_results.json scaled_hud. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: At200% text, let the opening next-step guidance appear while Stats/Build/Tech is active.
impact: Passive tutorial text competes with the active interface and forces extra scrolling for routine controls.
recommendation: Keep a short next-action line with optional expandable detail, and cap passive guidance height without clipping actionable/error messages.
acceptance: At supported text sizes, guidance leaves enough space for active content and can expand on request; full text remains accessible.

title: The sweep banner cannot take the player to the threatened branch
evidence: warn_banner uses MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE and displays countdown/hops only; alert actions have no sweep kind. Camera can be elsewhere when a sweep starts. Actual tracer geometry is separately owned by the map agent. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Pan away from the current trace path when ICE announces a sweep.
impact: The reaction timer runs while the player searches for the attacked branch and relevant link.
recommendation: Make the sweep headline a navigation action that focuses the current threatened edge/path and exposes available counteractions.
acceptance: One click/key action on the sweep warning finds the current trace path and explains the next threatened hop without disturbing unrelated topology.

title: Keep the pointed-at host stable when wheel-zooming
evidence: _zoom only changes camera.zoom and never adjusts camera.position. Therefore any world point away from the viewport centre moves away from the pointer during wheel zoom. Final source recheck: _zoom still changes scale without preserving the world point beneath the pointer.
reproduction: Place the pointer over a host near a map edge and zoom several wheel steps; the zoom centre remains the camera centre.
impact: Inspecting or placing precisely requires repeated camera correction after changing scale.
recommendation: Anchor wheel zoom to the current pointer's world point, subject to sensible world bounds.
acceptance: An in-bounds host remains beneath the pointer across zoom steps at all supported scales; keyboard or dedicated overview zoom remains predictable.

title: Bound camera travel and provide a quick return to C2
evidence: Keyboard, edge and drag panning directly add/subtract camera.position without a map-bound clamp. The world is only 2400x2400 pixels; camera navigation can continue into entirely empty space. Final source recheck: Pan/drag/edge updates still have no world clamp and no dedicated return-to-C2 control is present.
reproduction: Hold a pan key or edge-pan away from the map until its buildings leave view. This is a source-confirmed navigation possibility, not a performance conclusion from render-probe screenshots.
impact: A player can lose their network and spend time recovering instead of making routing decisions.
recommendation: Allow a small overscroll margin, clamp or softly stop beyond it, and add a visible/keybound return-to-C2 action.
acceptance: Ordinary panning cannot leave the map unrecoverably offscreen, and one action reliably returns C2 to the usable map viewport at any zoom.

title: Show currently accessible territory on the minimap
evidence: The minimap bakes all district colours with no _vision_list or _vis_blocks overlay, while placement requires every footprint cell to be within vision. Startup screenshots show the whole resource map despite only a small usable neighbourhood. Final source recheck: Minimap texture still colours all districts without the current access/vision overlay.
reproduction: At startup compare the fully coloured minimap with fog and legal placement reach around C2.
impact: Players can navigate toward resources on the overview without a cue that more access infrastructure is needed before acting there.
recommendation: Retain known district geography if desired, but add a clear current-access or discovered-area overlay using the same vision state as the world.
acceptance: The overview distinguishes accessible and unavailable territory through redundant visual cues and updates after a new host or Proxy extends reach.

title: Use the minimap to locate network health and the current selection
evidence: Every node is drawn as a fixed 3x3 resource-colour square. There is no disabled/offline/quarantined state, selected-node highlight, or active-sweep marker; screenshot 07's disabled producer is not distinguishable from an operational producer in the overview. Final source recheck: Canonical _op_state now exists for the inspector, but minimap markers still ignore it, selection and sweep position.
reproduction: Compare screenshots 06_selected_producer.png and 07_disabled_producer.png at the minimap, then review the node-marker draw loop.
impact: When the network grows, players cannot use the overview to find the selected branch or locate a failure without moving the main camera.
recommendation: Add compact redundant status/selection markers and an ICE position cue; dirty redraw only when those states change.
acceptance: Selection and disabled/offline/quarantined hosts can be distinguished without colour alone; active ICE can be located while its branch is offscreen.

title: Tunnel rendering repeatedly rebuilds stable route geometry
evidence: _draw queries _path_bounds for each tunnel; that function loops the route cells, and _edge_pts recreates route polylines. Packet movement has a _polyline cache, but bounds and drawing do not share it. This is a source-confirmed avoidable cost; no isolated savings estimate is claimed.
reproduction: Inspect draw work with long street routes while endpoints/topology remain fixed.
impact: Stable routes perform repeated allocation and cell traversal whenever ambient animation redraws the map.
recommendation: Cache bounds, rendered polyline and segment lengths together per topology revision; invalidate on reroute, removal and restore.
acceptance: Repeated draws allocate no fresh stable-route geometry; topology changes update all caches before rendering or movement.

title: Packet movement repeatedly searches long polylines from their start
evidence: CPU microbench using a synthetic winding120-cell/62-point path measured mean movement0.236ms at100 packets,2.715ms at1000 and9.235ms at3000(p95 13.647ms). _point_at_dist linearly searches segments and per-packet lookup repeats work. These counts are stress fixtures. Evidence: performance_results.json.
reproduction: Run the packet movement microbench at100/1000/3000 packets on the same winding path.
impact: Packet work competes with simulation and rendering as traffic grows.
recommendation: Cache cumulative segment distances and use a remembered segment index or binary search; reuse positions for drawing, with explicit reverse-direction handling.
acceptance: Movement is identical across bends and both directions, and the same packet fixture shows lower mean/p95 CPU time.

title: Full fog recomputation becomes a noticeable placement spike
evidence: Synthetic400-node CPU microbench measured mean vision rebuild40.25ms(max46.3ms), compared with cached check0.153ms. Rebuild tests fog block centres against the full host list; the cached path also scans every node for relays. Evidence: performance_results.json vision_rebuild/vision_cached.
reproduction: Compare cached and invalidated _vision_list timings at1/50/150/400 nodes; profile a node-set mutation.
impact: Adding/removing/converting a host can briefly stall feedback in a larger network.
recommendation: Track visibility revision explicitly and update only affected blocks using spatial buckets or coverage counts. Ensure Undo/load invalidates the correct region.
acceptance: Same fixture substantially reduces mutation-time spikes while visible cells and placement legality remain equivalent to the reference calculation.

title: The sidebar recomputes mostly unchanged telemetry every frame
evidence: Baseline v064 CPU microbench at400 synthetic nodes measured UI._process means1.92ms on Build and2.66ms on Stats per call. The UI walks network state and formats labels every frame while most simulation values change at10Hz or rate samples at1Hz. v065 adds compact-header measurement; quoted timings remain v064 measurements.
reproduction: Run UI process microbench on unchanged fixtures and inspect label assignments/network loops during paused frames.
impact: Large networks pay formatting/counting costs on frames that cannot display new information.
recommendation: Refresh telemetry on simulation/rate revisions, inspector state on selection/mutations and layout on scale/size changes. Keep hover and warnings responsive.
acceptance: Paused idle UI performs no unnecessary full-network telemetry pass; live values refresh at their data cadence and actions update immediately.

title: Paused frames still hash every node to detect visual changes
evidence: CPU microbench measured _visual_sig mean0.986ms at400 nodes even without state changes. It hashes a full per-node representation on each main._process call. Evidence: performance_results.json visual_signature; the main script is unchanged in v065.
reproduction: Profile stationary paused scenes at1/50/150/400 nodes and inspect _visual_sig.
impact: The existing repaint gate still spends proportional CPU time on an idle network.
recommendation: Increment a visual revision at every visible mutation and compare revisions; retain explicit camera/pointer/animation gates and audit all mutation paths.
acceptance: Paused idle detection is constant-time while toggles, selection, settings, Undo, threat state and restores still repaint once.

title: The Stats graph redraws every paused frame without new samples
evidence: Rendered paused Stats test recorded80 graph draw notifications across80 frames while time/history sampling was stopped. graph._process checks its local visible flag and calls queue_redraw each frame. Evidence: render_results.json paused_stats.
reproduction: Open Stats, pause, keep pointer/camera fixed and count graph draw notifications over80 frames.
impact: A static chart repeatedly regenerates identical drawing commands and may do work while an ancestor hides it.
recommendation: Redraw only on a history revision, size/theme/text-scale change or first becoming visible in the tree.
acceptance: Paused unchanged Stats produces zero repeated graph redraws; each new sample and layout change repaints promptly.

title: Simulation catch-up has no per-frame work budget
evidence: main._process drains all accumulated0.1s ticks in an unbounded while loop. Separate400-node CPU fixtures measured roughly13ms per tick; a hitch can therefore demand several costly ticks before input/rendering resumes. No observed shipping-frame hitch or spiral is claimed.
reproduction: Introduce controlled frame hitches in the isolated project and record catch-up work, elapsed simulation time and input latency.
impact: After a pause in execution, accumulated simulation work can extend the recovery stall.
recommendation: Set a documented per-frame catch-up/time budget and carry remaining debt across frames, with a clear policy for very long stalls. Preserve deterministic tick ordering.
acceptance: Controlled250ms/1s hitches recover with bounded input latency and no silently skipped resource, threat or contract time under the chosen policy.

title: Long-route cursor previews need a bounded work cadence
evidence: Existing cached A* preview CPU probe on a generated100x100 city measured mean0.558ms for nearby target,5.88ms to(79,79),6.41ms to(99,99). The heap/search cap improvements are already present; this is remaining synchronous work on changed pointer cells. Evidence: performance_results.json route_preview.
reproduction: Sweep the pointer through successive distant cells with a source armed; compare interactive latency with the recorded per-search microbench.
impact: Repeated long searches can make route placement feel sticky despite a working path cache.
recommendation: Debounce or budget preview work and cancel stale targets; render a pending state and validate the current endpoint synchronously on commit when needed.
acceptance: Long-route hover remains responsive, stale results never appear on newer targets, and commit cost/validity uses the current topology.

title: Account for route latency and supply rate in contract difficulty
evidence: The final snapshot filters stock offers by reachable output resources and allows Decline. Offer amount/deadline selection still does not budget for current production rate, input availability or end-to-end route latency. This is a balance proposal, not a recorded campaign deadline failure.
reproduction: Source comparison: the same 50-Intel/90-second contract can be offered to a short sustained route and a distant starved route without changing difficulty or reward.
impact: The contract challenge can be dominated by seed geography and travel time rather than a deliberate player improvement.
recommendation: Use a few simple contract tiers keyed to achieved production, with a travel allowance and clear risk classification; keep acceptance optional.
acceptance: Each tier has a feasible reference network, and the allowed time includes the first required packet round trip without relying on an unimplemented supply chain.

title: Align coverage tuning with the actual radius-four grid ceiling
evidence: A radius-four integer disk intersects at most seven distinct 3x3 occupied blocks on a four-cell grid across all 16 centre phases. Thus current coverage/5 tops out at 1.4 before vacancies/farm narrowing, while the clamp/comment allow 2.5. Final source recheck: Radius, four-cell blocks, integer disk and coverage/5 are unchanged; the seven-building, 1.4 upper-bound proof still applies.
reproduction: Read findings/coverage_geometry.json: exhaustive fully occupied-grid upper-bound calculation reproduces _coverage disk and block layout; no Godot playthrough is claimed.
impact: The advertised tuning range above 1.4 is unreachable in the current geometry, which distorts balance assumptions for advanced production and placement rewards.
recommendation: Choose an attainable density reference divisor or lower the documented/tuned upper range; avoid enlarging the radius solely to justify an old number.
acceptance: The stated production multiplier range is reachable on a documented legal dense placement and verified by a small seed sample; sparse placements remain useful.

title: Separate victory progress from the wallet spent on upgrades
evidence: The win check uses resources.credits >= 1000, while advanced facilities and tunnels deduct that same wallet. Every investment immediately reduces displayed goal progress even when it improves the network. Final source recheck: Victory still uses current credits >= 1000; facility and tunnel Cash purchases reduce that same wallet.
reproduction: At a high Cash balance, buy a Cloud Cryptojacker, Mixer or HTTP tunnel; the victory balance falls by its cost.
impact: Near the finish, waiting with an adequate network can be more appealing than using the unlocked construction choices.
recommendation: Evaluate a cumulative earned-Cash milestone or a one-time final operation funded from Cash; keep Cash as the spendable currency.
acceptance: A successful upgrade does not erase completed objective progress, and the goal clearly communicates whether earnings, retained balance or a final spend is required.

title: Make compromised hosts look acquired rather than newly constructed
evidence: STRUCT supplies roof, windows, tiers and height for player nodes; _draw_building constructs architecture over the static city. The same physical-building metaphor dominates both unowned and owned map objects. Final source recheck: Player nodes still use tiered architecture, roof and window profiles. Canonical inspector operational-state labels do not change ownership rendering.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: compare _paint_city background blocks with the tier/roof rendering of a deployed producer.
impact: Neon decoration does not clearly communicate the change from remote target to controlled host.
recommendation: Keep the city backdrop and footprint, but present acquired endpoints as marked hosts or executable modules with an unmistakable compromised state and resource glyph.
acceptance: Before/after ownership can be identified at normal and far zoom without relying on colour; High Contrast and Reduced Motion preserve the cue.

title: Permit a small set of producer upgrades that preserve the route
evidence: Higher-tier producers are separate placement tools. Replacing an existing footprint requires removal, and _remove_node detaches its incoming children and destroys their out-links. Final source recheck: Promote replacement: begin_reroute changes an existing edge, not producer type. Replacing a producer still requires removal, which detaches its children.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: replace a routing producer with a stronger same-resource producer; removal detaches connected child links.
impact: Research offers more production choices, but adopting them can demand repeated rewiring instead of improving an established network.
recommendation: Support only obvious same-resource upgrades, charge the upgrade cost, and preserve footprint, parent route and incoming links when compatible.
acceptance: An upgraded Cycles or Intel host retains valid network connections, recalculates load/output, and remains reversible through the existing undo model.

title: Make Onion Routing's long-reach promise measurable
evidence: All five TUNNEL_MAXLEN entries equal 255. Onion Routing is described as long-reach but currently differs through loss/upkeep/capacity rather than a larger routing budget. Final source recheck: Every TUNNEL_MAXLEN remains 255; long-route niche recommendation is still valid.
reproduction: Compare _tool_maxlen for DNS, VPN, Reverse Shell, HTTP and Onion; all return the same maximum route length.
impact: The advanced unlock does not communicate a clearly distinct reach capability, so a costly Tool-based purchase can disappoint the stated expectation.
recommendation: Give Onion one clear distance niche, such as a larger route budget or strongly improved long-route economics, and describe that exact benefit.
acceptance: A documented route comparison demonstrates a useful Onion advantage that another early protocol does not already provide at lower total cost.

title: Make going quiet a meaningful answer to escalating pursuit
evidence: notoriety uses max(previous, wealth)+0.03 per second, never decays, and can independently charge sweeps above 45 even when Trace is zero. DDoS resets Trace and charge but not notoriety. Final source recheck: Notoriety still never decays and independently charges sweeps. New reroute affordance adds active evasion but does not make quieting prevent notoriety-driven pursuit.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: once notoriety exceeds 45, use silent DNS/VPN links and zero Trace; _update_sweep still accumulates pursuit charge.
impact: Quiet protocol choices eventually stop preventing pursuit, while the game's guidance frames quieting as a defensive response.
recommendation: Either let sustained low exposure reduce pursuit pressure, or explicitly teach that permanent reputation requires active evasion rather than quieting.
acceptance: A low-exposure strategy has a documented effect on future sweep frequency, or the independent reputation threat is clearly introduced before it becomes irreversible.

title: Stop optional Labs consuming inputs after the last useful unlock
evidence: TECH contains a finite seven-entry tree. _sim_tick continues Lab pulls and fuel spending after all technologies are researched; Research has no further spend in the current game. Final source recheck: Lab consumption still runs after the finite TECH set is fully unlocked; no auto-standby or repeatable Research use was added.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: mark all TECH entries researched, retain an enabled linked Lab with Intel and Cycles, then evaluate processor pulls.
impact: A completed research system can keep diverting the resources needed for the remaining Cash objective without producing usable value.
recommendation: Put Labs in automatic standby when no current Research spend remains, with an explicit resume option for continued sandbox stockpiling.
acceptance: After the last unlock, ordinary Lab automation stops consuming Intel/Cycles and clearly reports standby; manual override and saves preserve the intended state.

title: Give the central Spire a simple end-of-run purpose
evidence: Generation always creates a Spire with ICE tier 3, but ZONE_RES gives it no output and victory checks only the Cash balance. It provides no unique operation or completion condition. Final source recheck: Spire remains an ICE-3 district with no unique completion operation; Cash is still the only win check.
reproduction: Compare the Spire's generation/security entries with _placement_error, producer resource mappings and the win check.
impact: The visually prominent centre promises a destination that the economy does not require the player to reach.
recommendation: Add one optional or final Spire operation using existing Tools, routing and Cash rather than adding a separate progression currency.
acceptance: The Spire has a stated actionable purpose and visible completion result; a player can understand its requirements before committing to the route.

title: Validate an accessible starter route for each generated map
evidence: _place_hub selects the first residential coarse cell from the left. Generation does not validate reachable legal producer footprints, nearby Intel access, or the cost of the first useful reveal route. Final source recheck: Generation and first-residential hub placement remain unvalidated for a guaranteed affordable opening route.
reproduction: Source review of generation and hub placement; inspect a fixed seed set for legal starter Cycles/Intel paths and required spend.
impact: Procedural variation can change the cost and clarity of the first lesson before the player understands routing; frequency needs a seed sweep, not a claimed played failure.
recommendation: Validate a small opening neighbourhood and reroll or adjust only invalid starts, preserving the rest of the random city.
acceptance: A documented seed batch always offers a legal Cycles foothold and an affordable path toward Intel using starting resources and early income.

title: Market saturation immediately reverses when the player spends Cash
evidence: Measured controlled wallet fixture: at1000 Cash quote0.50; spending500 Cash raises quote0.75 without a change in sales volume. _market_price depends solely on present resources.credits. Evidence: simulation_results wallet_market_price. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Compare sale quote before and after buying Cash-costing infrastructure.
impact: The description says sales saturate demand, but buying upgrades restores demand instantly; the intended diversification incentive is weak and hard to understand.
recommendation: Choose wallet-sensitive pricing deliberately and explain it, or base saturation on cumulative/recent sales with an explicit recovery mechanism.
acceptance: A spending-only action has the documented pricing effect; market-demand changes can be explained from visible inputs.

title: Startup menu has no initial keyboard focus
evidence: menu._ready creates buttons but never selects a focus target. The real-scene probe records initial_focus.path='null'. Keyboard Tab can initiate navigation; this proposal improves immediate discoverability rather than claiming keyboard navigation is impossible. Final source recheck: Replace resolved CONTROLS02 with this startup-focus proposal. _ready still never focuses a startup action; _open_settings focuses Reduced motion only after the new modal opens.
reproduction: Launch using a keyboard and look for a focused default action before pressing Tab.
impact: There is no visible starting point or immediately actionable default for keyboard users.
recommendation: Focus Continue when a usable save is available, otherwise New Game, and retain a clear focus indicator.
acceptance: The entry menu has one sensible initial focus target; Enter/Space activates it and all actions remain reachable with Tab/Shift+Tab.

title: The Cash chart has no time or value scale
evidence: Viewed screenshot10_stats.png and graph.gd: only 'Cash→1000 goal' is drawn; samples are arolling120-entry one-Hz buffer. No timestamps,x-axis range,value ticks or hover values are available. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Open Stats after several minutes of play and interpret a rising/falling segment.
impact: The chart's meaning and measurement window cannot be read reliably, making economic comparisons guesswork.
recommendation: Label the rolling time window and currency scale; add current/peak values or simple hover readouts appropriate to a small sparkline. Use an adaptive early-game range with an explicit goal marker so small improvements remain visible; label the chosen range.
acceptance: A player can determine the chart's period, approximate balance and timing of changes without reading code. Early Cash changes are discernible and the player can tell the displayed time span and value range.

title: Preserve map proportions in the minimap
evidence: The actual 1280x720 startup layout reports a 284x148 minimap for a square 100x100 map. Its texture and coordinates scale independently on each axis, stretching horizontal relationships by about 1.92 relative to vertical ones; screenshots 02 and 20 show this wide projection. Final source recheck: Minimap draw/click transforms and 284x148 UI size are unchanged; aspect-distortion finding remains.
reproduction: Compare a square district/camera footprint in the world with its displayed minimap proportions in 02_new_game.png.
impact: Distances and neighbourhood shapes on the overview do not match the spatial relationships used for routing.
recommendation: Letterbox a square map area inside the existing control and share its transform between drawing and click-to-pan.
acceptance: Equal world distances appear equal on both minimap axes, and clicks map correctly through any letterbox margins.

title: Allow players to replay and share a map seed
evidence: The main menu assigns randi() for every New Game. Session.seed is already consumed by main and the current seed is available in Stats, but there is no seed-entry or restart-same-seed action. Final source recheck: Promote replacement: New Game still assigns randi(), with no seed field or restart-same-seed action. Menu Accessibility additions do not provide map replay.
reproduction: Source walkthrough of New Game and Session.seed consumption; the current menu always selects a new random seed.
impact: Players cannot easily retry a difficult layout, compare routing solutions or reproduce an interesting city.
recommendation: Offer an optional seed field and a restart-this-map action; retain random New Game as the default.
acceptance: Entering the same seed produces the same layout and start, and the chosen seed can be copied without accessing save files.
